method: Class breaks turn a column of values into the handful of shades a choropleth map can carry. Equal interval divides the full span into k classes of the same width, w = (max - min) / k, with breaks at min + i*w, so every class covers the same number of units and the map reads directly in the data's own unit; a single large value, however, stretches the first class until nearly every area falls inside it. Quantile sorts the values and reads the breaks at i/k of the way through the order statistics, with linear interpolation between neighbouring values - the type 7 definition of Hyndman and Fan, which is the default in R's quantile() and NumPy's percentile - so each class holds roughly the same count; the cost is that the value width of each class varies with the data and the map hides the true spacing. Both methods return k+1 breaks including the minimum and the maximum. Breaks are rounded to six significant figures of the data range before the values are counted: the decimal places are 6 - floor(log10(max - min)), clamped to 0 through 12, so a range in the hundreds keeps four decimals, a range in the billions keeps none and a range in millionths keeps twelve. A value joins the class whose lower bound it meets or exceeds and whose upper bound it falls below, so a value sitting exactly on an interior break joins the class above it; the top class also includes the maximum. Counts and shares follow from the rounded breaks, which keeps the table self-consistent. Duplicate values that straddle a break leave the class between them empty, and that is reported rather than hidden; a class holding more than half of the values (with at least three classes and eight values) raises a note, and fewer than two values per class warns that quantile breaks sit on individual values. Inputs accept 2 to 5000 values separated by commas, semicolons, spaces or new lines, each with up to six decimals and no exponent notation, within -1,000,000,000 to 1,000,000,000; the class count is a whole number from 2 to 9. Blank, malformed, out-of-range and single-value lists are refused with a field-specific message, and a list whose values are all identical is refused because no classification exists. Natural breaks (Jenks), geometric intervals, standard-deviation breaks, areal weighting, projection and geometry are out of scope. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Cynthia A. Brewer, Designing Better Maps: A Guide for GIS Users - quantile and equal-interval class intervals for choropleth maps, their trade-offs, and the practical limit of five to seven shades.

Hyndman and Fan (1996), Sample Quantiles in Statistical Packages, The American Statistician 50(4) - the type 7 quantile definition, linear interpolation between order statistics, used for the quantile breaks.
QGIS and ArcGIS documentation for graduated classification - equal interval and quantile break methods, lower-inclusive class bounds, and the legend ranges they produce.
